summary: Redwood team walked ByteWave through Optimize quantization profiles (INT8 and FP8). Focus was on quality vs latency tradeoffs, expected token cost reductions, and deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC). ByteWave is interested in a short pilot to validate quality on their prompt set and evaluate latency SLOs for low-latency chat use cases.
transcript:
[00:00] Sara (AE): Hey everyone good afternoon, thanks for joining. We got about 60 minutes, want to do a short overview then deep dive into quant profiles - INT8 and FP8 - and then leave time for questions. Mike?
[00:12] Mike (ByteWave CTO): Yeah thanks. We mostly want to understand the latency impact and risk to hallucination/quality if we move to INT8 or FP8. Our product is conversational support so sub-200ms is a goal for short queries.
[00:22] Daniel (SE): Quick note - when we say FP8 here we're talking about our tuned FP8 profile for decoder-only open models; INT8 tends to be more aggressive on size but may need more eval tuning. We ran the numbers on a 7B-like baseline and saw token cost reductions around 40-60% for INT8 and 30-45% for FP8 depending on sequence length.
[00:38] Priya (ML Eng): Are those numbers on your hosted fleet or a dedicated GPU pool? Because our infra team will need to know scheduling and pre-warm time.
[00:45] Daniel: Those were on Dedicated with our optimized kernels. On hosted the delta is similar but absolute latency is slightly higher due to multi-tenant scheduling. For dedicated we measured median token-latency reductions of ~1.6x with INT8 across our benchmark, and FP8 typically gives a 1.3x improvement with less quality risk.
[01:05] Ava (Infra): Are we looking at KV cache compatibility? We heavily use long-context caching.
[01:10] Jen (SE): Yes, KV cache is supported in both quant profiles; our runtime preserves KV layout. There are a couple micro-differences on the kernel path that can slightly change peak memory usage, but we handle this in the profile and the optimizer will pick the kernel variant automatically.
[01:28] Mike: Can you show an example where INT8 fails or degrades output? That's the main concern for us.
[01:34] Daniel: Sure, we'll show a couple prompts. Note transcription: sometimes model names get munged - it's our internal 'rw-opt' profile. Example 1 - a factual extraction: INT8 produced a slightly truncated numerics answer in one out of 1000 queries on our set; FP8 matched baseline in that case. Example 2 - creative generation: INT8 introduced mild repetitions more often. But with our post-quant calibration and a hint of mixed-precision fallback for certain layers, we can recover quality while keeping most of the performance wins.
[02:10] [Screen share starts - Daniel shows dashboard]
[02:18] Daniel: Here is the Optimize dashboard - per-model quant profiles, quality regressions by prompt-set, and latency histograms. This is a sample for '7b-chat-like' model. You can see on the left the quality-vs-latency slider; we export CSVs with aggregated BLEU/ROUGE or task-specific metrics.
[02:42] Priya: What's the expected change in tail latency? Our SLA is 95th <= 300ms for conversational flows.
[02:49] Daniel: Good question. For median tokens we see the numbers I mentioned; at 95th percentile the improvements are smaller because tail is influenced by batching, network hop and cache misses. For dedicated with optimal batching and prefix caching we achieved 95th of ~1.15x improvement for FP8 and ~1.35x for INT8 in our internal tests on similar workloads. You'll want to run your prompt set because distribution matters a lot.
[03:15] Mike: Ok, what about hallucination / safety regressions? Do you run evals?
[03:20] Liam (Product): Yeah we tie regressions to eval suites - when a quant profile triggers a significant drop we flag it and recommend either mixed precision or fallback to higher-precision on that route. The Optimize console will show per-prompt deltas and allow you to pin a model/version per route.
[03:40] Priya: Are the evals customizable? We have a few proprietary prompt sets.
[03:44] Daniel: Absolutely - you can upload your own prompts and ground truths; the system computes task-specific metrics and flags quality regressions. That's actually what we'd like to run in the pilot.
[03:56] Carlos (SRE): From a security standpoint we need to review KMS and network flow. We can't have tokens exfil.
[04:02] Jen: Understood - for Private/Dedicated we offer VPC peering and customer-managed KMS; logs and audit trails are retained per your retention policy. We'll share SOC2 and the KMS architecture doc.
[04:18] Ava: Great, please send that. Also latency between our cluster and your helm is a factor - we may need on-prem.
[04:25] Daniel: We support on-prem or VPC/private deployments; for on-prem there is an extra prep for kernel compatibility but the quant profiles themselves are the same.
[04:36] [Daniel navigates to CSV export]
[04:40] Daniel: Here are side-by-side quality-vs-latency charts. This scatterplot shows prompt-level delta: x-axis is latency improvement, y-axis is quality delta; points in top-right are wins. You can filter by tag, route, or prompt-type. For ByteWave's conversational set we'd expect most prompts to land in mild improvement zone but a small tail may show quality drops with INT8.
[05:05] Priya: Can you quantify "small tail"?
[05:08] Daniel: In our experience about 1-3% of prompts saw >5% metric drop for INT8 on a conversational extraction task; FP8 reduced that to <1% usually. Those numbers vary by model and prompt.
[05:22] Mike: Sounds reasonable. For cost, what are we looking at? If INT8 reduces tokens by 50% we can reallocate infra spend.
[05:29] Sara: Our estimate is unit token cost reduction 35-55% for INT8 depending on model; FP8 around 25-40%. We'll provide model-by-model costing in the report. Also note that batching and cache tuning in Redwood Optimize can add further gains.
[05:45] Ava: For the pilot, we'd prefer a dedicated pool with VPC peering so traffic stays internal. How long to provision?
[05:51] Jen: For dedicated pool with basic setup we can provision in 3-5 business days after contract; VPC peering adds a couple days for networking. Pilot plan: 2 weeks of testing with your prompt set, we'll run before/after evals and handoff results.
[06:06] Mike: Ok let's scope the pilot. We want to test 3 models: 7B-chat, 13B instruction, and a tuned 13B that we use for summarization. Objective: maintain quality delta <2% on our metrics and push latency below 250ms median if possible.
[06:20] Daniel: That works. We'll propose config: start with FP8 profile to get conservative wins, then trial INT8 on a subset of traffic with canary routing and autosafe fallback if quality drops sense.
[06:33] Priya: Canary routing - how granular is that?
[06:36] Liam: Per-route and per-user canaries; you can ramp 1% -> 10% -> 50% automatically and have regression alerts tied to eval thresholds.
[06:45] Mike: Good. Also curious about model rollbacks - do you version the quant profiles?
[06:49] Daniel: Yes, profiles and model versions are immutable once promoted; you can create new profiles and rollback. The console tracks changes and shows diff on metrics.
[07:00] [Short pause - questions from Mike and Priya about specific prompt examples]
[07:20] Daniel: Here's a real example. Prompt: 'Summarize the following support ticket and extract root cause.' Baseline answer length 120 tokens. INT8 produced an answer with slightly different ordering and missed one sub-root cause in 0.8% of runs. FP8 matched baseline. We can mitigate by per-route mixed precision for the extraction head.
[07:48] Priya: That mitigation - is it automatic?
[07:51] Daniel: We have a suggestion engine. It will propose layer-level mixed precision or fallback rules, but you can enforce them.
[08:00] Ava: If we go on-prem, what support level do you provide?
[08:04] Sara: Enterprise support plus an on-site or remote runbook for kernel compatibility. Also SRE handoff for onboarding.
[08:12] Mike: Alright let's talk timeline. We aim to decide by next Wednesday.
[08:16] Sara: We'll follow up with pricing, the quant report, and a benchmark plan. Proposed kickoff 12/13.
[08:22] Daniel: I'll need the sample prompt set and 1-2 representative routes to reproduce your latency profile.
[08:28] Priya: We'll upload via the secure upload link you sent earlier.
[08:32] Jen: We'll also include a short how-to on running the per-prompt evals locally.
[08:38] [Wrap-up and confirmations]
[08:42] Sara: To recap - we're sharing the quant report and pricing, Daniel will run a ByteWave-sized benchmark, and we'll schedule the pilot kickoff if ByteWave signs. Any last questions?
[08:50] Mike: None from me. Appreciate the thoroughness.
[08:53] Priya: No, thanks.
[08:55] Sara: Great, we'll follow up early next week. Thanks everyone.
[08:59] [Meeting ends]
